Everything the branch claims about semantics and the record stream holds, with one exception. I verified the engine fence by tree hash (all four crates identical, not just stat-clean), then reproduced the "zero behavior change" claim independently rather than trusting the T8 review: the same seeded 2P sim game driven 4000 steps through the master and HEAD binaries produced byte-identical 3200-event records and terminal digests, and the same live 2P setup entered through both (differently-worded) wizards produced identical setup_observations, choices, config, events and digest. Wave-2 choreography survives verbatim — the only diffs in those tests are `0`->`1` and `k`->`menu_number(k)` from the numbering ruling — and I re-derived each property on the shipped binary rather than only reading the tests: mid-group abort leaves the record object bit-identical, reveals precede their move in one group, undo removes the whole group, a persisted lockdown reloads locked and blocks everything but save/log/quit, `suggest` repeats byte-identically and records nothing, and undo's bot attribution is identical with and without a save/quit/reload cycle. `stream_seed`, `undo_cmd`, `pump_bots_with`, the desync guards and `bot.rs`'s honest chain are byte-identical to master modulo prose dashes.

THE FINDING came from the one genuinely new affordance: T8 made six full-screen views reachable from inside a live reveal capture, but `view_render::exit_line()` stayed context-free and still promises "a NUMBER applies that option, and 'back' undoes your last move". At a capture a number is an order-card ID, so obeying the footer records a card identity and commits the parked move. The branch had already solved this on the index side (`IndexContext`) and already knows the clause is false there (`the_capture_prompt_is_the_composed_reveal_zone` asserts the capture's own hint must not carry it) — the behavior pin just never left the main prompt.

NEAR MISSES I chased and did not file. (1) `ports`/`labs` opened mid-capture render the PRE-move display while the capture asks about a POST-refill slot number — genuinely confusing at the table, but it is the honest consequence of atomicity (nothing is applied yet) and the prompt says so, so I judged it design rather than defect; it is the strongest candidate for a follow-up if the owner hits it at the gate. (2) `reveal_cmd`'s new card pre-check now runs ahead of the engine, so a bad card plus a non-hidden seat or a finished game yields the card refusal where master gave the seat/game-over one — refuses either way, records nothing. (3) A hidden seat's panel line reads "0 orders in hand (hidden)" while that seat physically holds a card; both master and HEAD read `order_cards_in_hand.len()`, so this is pre-existing engine representation, not a branch change. (4) Under lockdown, `log` renders in the pre-redesign compact shape rather than the full-screen view — deliberate, documented at repl.rs:597 and pinned by `the_log_still_reads_under_a_lockdown`. (5) `assert_no_ascii_prose_dash` matches only `" -- "`, so a dash without both spaces would slip — presentation sweep, outside this lens. On the named check specifically, I audited every `.contains` needle in reveal.rs and session.rs and found one dead needle (filed as the NOTE); the reveal, lockdown, suggest and seat-identity pins I read are anchored to whole cells or backed by `assert_eq!` and are not satisfiable by a neighbouring line.

lenses.summary:
I attacked the leak fence from the model, the shipped binary, and mutation, and could not make it disclose anything a seated player cannot know. The two things I am filing are both NOTEs and both about honesty-of-presentation rather than an actual disclosure.

What I did. Verified HEAD `31336c5` and the empty engine fence first and last. Drove the real binary three ways: piped with no controlling TTY, piped from inside a 210-column Forge PTY, and interactively in that PTY (4P sim with a bot at seat 2, and a full live 2P wizard with hidden deals). Built a scratch worktree at HEAD and wrote three sweeps: (a) every surface the driver can render — frame, 13 view-menu targets, all four indexes, both reveal stages — greped for every unrevealed order id at 2/3/4P live with hidden seats at both privacy settings, and for every other seat's held card at 2/3/4P sim with privacy on and with a bot; (b) a model-level pass asserting no index annotates a card in `order_deck ∪ orders_removed` or in another seat's hand; (c) a probe of a real parked live port-refill capture dumping every annotation and all three refusal classes at both privacy settings. Proved each sweep non-vacuous by mutation, then removed the worktree and closed the terminal.

Two mis-reads I made and corrected, worth stating so they are not repeated: the order index legitimately lists all 36 registry cards, so an id appearing there is the index doing its job — only a LOCATION annotation counts; and `card_prompt`'s entry hint prints a literal example id `'O14'`, which false-positived against a fixture whose hidden card happened to be O14.

Near-misses I chose not to file. (1) `privacy` does not toggle while a reveal capture or a Movement sub-prompt is pending — `Repl::step` routes the line to the collector, which refuses it as a card (`'privacy' is not a card…`). Deliberate modality, pre-existing, loudly refused, and the dangerous direction is already the default in live (privacy ON), so I could not build a scenario where it discloses. (2) The sim wizard shows every seat's dealt PAIR, including a seat later assigned to a bot, because the keep questions precede the bot-seats question — pre-existing at master and exactly what `render.rs:30-34` disclaims, so the bot hand mask is hygiene rather than a barrier by design. (3) `bot_hand_is_masked_regardless_of_privacy` asserts `panel_hand_line(&open, 0).contains('O')` — a single-character needle that bites today only because no uppercase O appears in the mask string; one rewording of `masked_hand` (say to "1 Order card (hidden…)") makes it vacuous. Too speculative to file as a defect, but it is the named class and cheap to harden. (4) In live mode `index_placements` and the `hand` view call the CURRENT player's hand "yours", which at an opponent's turn with privacy off is the wrong pronoun — but a live seat's hand holds only publicly-taken cards plus a revealed starting order, so there is nothing hidden behind the wrong word.

The gate-game configuration specifically (live 2P, privacy defaulting ON, one hidden opponent) came out clean on every check: the hidden seat's hand is structurally empty until revealed, the frame and every view carry counts only, the index annotates nothing unrevealed, and the reveal prompt's refusals fall back to the pool wording exactly as T8 claims.
verified_clean: Engine fence: `git diff --stat master..HEAD -- crates/yokohama-core crates/yokohama-oracle crates/yokohama-difftest crates/gen-data` is empty, checked at the start and again at the end of the pass.

Piped byte-identity: the same 56-line live-2P wizard+probe script produces byte-identical output (73,054 bytes, md5 9b7aa6614e466a9d99877e0627c8f975) whether run with no controlling TTY (Bash tool) or piped from inside a 210-column PTY where `/dev/tty` and `stty size` both answer — so `screen::terminal_width`'s `may_measure` fence, the color gate and the editor gate all stay disarmed in a pipe. Zero ESC bytes in both.

Editor gate clause 2 (stdin on a real TTY, stdout redirected to a file): 3,360 bytes, ZERO ESC bytes, no composed frame, and the standing hint drops the `↑ recalls what you typed` clause — i.e. `input::may_edit()` is false and no rustyline redraw reaches the redirected stream.

Readline history is in-memory only, checked three independent ways: `cargo tree -p yokohama-cli -e normal` resolves rustyline 18.0.1 with no `home`/`dirs`/`fd-lock` crate (so `with-file-history` is off and `DefaultHistory` is `MemHistory`); in a real `pty.fork()` session a distinctive token IS recalled by a genuine `\x1b[A` within the session (4 occurrences) and is NOT recalled by three `\x1b[A` presses in a freshly spawned process; and no file under $HOME (incl. `.zsh_history`), `~/.cache`, `~/.config`, `~/.local`, `~/Library/Application Support` or `/tmp` contains either sentinel, with no new file created in the window.

Card-index location annotations, swept at the MODEL level over all four registries at 2/3/4P: no index annotates a card still in `order_deck ∪ orders_removed` (live, seat 0 known + all others hidden, privacy on AND off), and none annotates another seat's held card (sim, privacy on AND off, with a bot seat). Non-vacuous — replacing `index_placements`' `if !self.seat_display().hides_hand(me)` gate with an all-seats loop makes both sweeps fail (12 annotations across 2/3/4P) and also fails 2 shipped tests.

A live hidden seat contributes literally nothing: `game/setup.rs:254-258`'s `StartingOrderChoice::Unknown` arm pushes BOTH dealt cards into `orders_removed` and leaves `order_cards_in_hand` empty, so there is no identity for the frame, the panels, the indexes or the reveal prompt to leak. Confirmed on the shipped binary — a live 2P wizard with both deals `hidden` prints `Seat 0 deal: hidden / Seat 1 deal: hidden` in its setup review and no dealt id anywhere in the 30 KB transcript.

Guided-reveal refusal wordings at a real live port-refill capture: with the hand MASKED (live default) a card in the current player's hand gets the POOL wording `O27 is not an unrevealed order card (not in the deck or the boxed/removed pile).`; with privacy off the same card gets the LOCATION wording `O27 is in your hand — a card cannot be in two places.`; a display card gets `O25 is Port A slot 1 — …`; the genuine deck card is accepted. No wording distinguishes an unrevealed card by where it actually is, and `index_placements` gains its `OwnHand` entry only when the toggle is open.

The players panel cannot name a card in either arrangement, structurally: `PlayerModel` carries `orders_in_hand: usize` and no card identity at all, so `panel_render::president_line` (beside/2P) and `seat_tail_row` (below/3-4P) can only ever print a count plus `(hidden)`. That is the R9 model seam rather than renderer discipline.

`screen_model::build_hand` masks in the MODEL (`cards: Vec::new()` when hidden) and both the frame's hand panel and the `hand` view build it for `state.current_player` with `SeatDisplay::hides_hand` already folded; `screen::stage` passes `state.current_player` in BOTH the beside and the below branches.

Bot-seat masking is independent of the privacy toggle — `Repl::seat_display` computes `self.privacy || self.bots.is_bot(seat)` — verified on the shipped binary at 4P sim with privacy at its OFF default: the bot column reads `1 order (hidden)` on the frame and `1 card (hidden — bot seat)` in `players`, with the distinct wording (never `'privacy' to toggle`) that keeps the toggle from being a false promise.

`suggest` refuses LIVE mode outright and refuses a seat a bot is playing; the continuation it prints is the suggesting seat's own turn to the hand-over, and it takes `&self` so it cannot record or autosave.

No CLI code reads `order_deck` / `tech_deck` / `orders_removed` for identities — only `.len()` (`PortsPanel.deck_remaining`, `LabsPanel.deck_remaining`, `delta_summary`'s deck-size lines) and membership in `reveal::check_order_reveal` / `check_tech_reveal`. Verified by grepping every occurrence in `crates/yokohama-cli/src/*.rs` and reading each production site.

`CardLocation` has no `Hand { seat }` variant, and every wording in `describe::card_location` (repl-side `Deal`/`PortSlot`/`OwnHand`/`ThisReveal`/`LabSlot`/`OwnedBy`/`OnArea`/`AchievementSlot`) names a face-up place or the operator's own recording context.

`CardPrompt::candidates` is `None` at every production call site (`card_prompt::orders`/`techs`, `reveal.rs:223`, `repl.rs:1665`, `wizard.rs:217`); the only `Some(..)` is in a unit test, so no prompt's refusal enumerates a pool.

`delta_summary`'s per-seat `hand +Oxx` / `hand -Oxx` lines are ungated by privacy, but they report only publicly-observable transfers (a face-up port take, an order completion, the reveal event itself) and are byte-unchanged from master — the branch touched neither the function nor its behaviour.

lenses.summary:
Ran 20 mutations across the branch's most load-bearing new pins (width equalities, the three swept maxima, the clip unit pin, the stride equality, per-seat hidden markers, the reveal-hint line pin, the pager partition, all 13 checked goldens, parser unit pins, the recall/history pins, the guide_sync §5/§8 pins, the leak fence, the log-actor routing). Seventeen were caught, usually by more than one test and usually with a message that names the fix. Three survived, one of which matters.

The one that matters is the LOCKDOWN allow-list (finding 1): a sixth recurrence of the NAMED CHECK, on the desync guard. `contains("locked")` cannot distinguish a refusal from an acceptance because every locked screen appends `lockdown_status()`, and the branch's own test at repl.rs:4186 proves the needle is present on an ACCEPTED command. The discriminating sweep exists (repl.rs:4190, needle "session locked") but covers five view words; `undo` — which rewinds the record — walks through untouched.

Near-misses I did not report. (a) `assert_no_ascii_prose_dash` matches only a space-flanked " -- ", so a line-terminal `--` escapes the rule; I found no instance at HEAD, so it is a shape observation rather than a defect. (b) The 14 `t12-*.txt` captures have no `assert_capture` caller — they are Forge-pass artifacts, and the ledger records them as such; the 13 real goldens are all live. (c) `no_module_hardcodes_the_customs_cost_progression` sweeps 5 of ~12 CLI modules, but its literal is specific and its anti-vacuity clause is genuine, so I let it stand. (d) The numeric-pick arm of `locked_mode_allows_only_...` IS saved by its state-equality assert — only the view-word arm is vacuous, which is why I anchored the finding at line 4573. (e) I could not demonstrate organic reachability for the pager caller gap: a temporary probe over 6,400 decisions (8 seed/rotation walks at 2/3/4P, up to 51 rows at a point) found zero page-count disagreements even with the caller mutated, so that one is a NOTE. (f) Every `force(false)`-then-assert site in the crate was scanned for the T11 paint-after-force degeneration; the fixed one (decision_render.rs:2030) now computes its tone inside the forced window with an explicit anti-vacuity assert, and every other site captures its painted string before the reset. All mutations reverted with `touch` + rebuild; final state: cli lib 594 / guide_sync 15 / 2 ignored green, engine fence empty vs master, `git status --porcelain` empty.
verified_clean: Capture goldens regenerate byte-identical from the shipped renderer: `UPDATE_CAPTURES=1 cargo test -p yokohama-cli --lib` -> 594 passed and `git status --porcelain docs/plans/.../captures/` EMPTY across all 13 checked goldens (t2/t3/t5/t6 x4/t10 x2/t11 x5). The compare direction bites too: flipping one 'RED'->'RAD' in t3-frame-2p.txt fails `screen::capture::the_committed_frame_capture_is_what_the_screen_renders` with a full diff.

Swept achievements maximum is a binding equality, not a bound: widening `achievements_row`'s separator by one column (panel_render.rs:1393) drives the 3P sweep to 174 and FAILS `the_widest_legal_achievements_row_survives_its_block_at_both_counts` (panel_render.rs:2352) with the exact 'RE-MEASURE BELOW_BLOCK_MIN' message.
Swept tracks maximum bites: widening the mercenary tail (panel_render.rs:1359) FAILS `the_widest_legal_tracks_row_survives_its_block_at_both_counts`.
Swept seat-tail maximum bites at its stated one column of margin: widening `next take` (panel_render.rs:1308) FAILS `the_widest_legal_seat_tail_row_still_fits_its_column`.

`header_row`'s clip unit pin is the ONLY thing covering that branch, and it holds: replacing `line_at(&t, width)` with the unclipped painted string fails exactly 1 of 38 panel_render tests — `an_over_wide_compressed_row_is_clipped_to_its_block_not_overrun` (panel_render.rs:2508) — reproducing the T10 review's 'delete the clip, 569 green' finding and showing the pin now closes it.

Stride is a real equality against the block-derived width, not a floor: replacing `let col_w = (width / seats).max(SEAT_COL_W)` with the bare constant (panel_render.rs:1018) FAILS `the_below_arrangement_is_aligned_fixed_height_and_legend_first` — the 3P cell (175/3 = 58 vs the constant's 50) is the one with grip, as documented.

Per-seat `(hidden)` is pinned per-line and counts occurrences: over-drawing the marker (`if p.hand_hidden || p.orders_in_hand > 0`) FAILS `the_hidden_marker_is_drawn_on_exactly_the_masked_seats_tail_row` on the two OPEN seats, and its `next take` anti-vacuity assert is real.

The reveal-hint pin reads the hint LINE, not the zone: appending `"'view' any surface"` to `reveal_hint`'s clause list (decision_render.rs:1137) FAILS `the_reveal_hint_never_offers_the_one_word_that_does_not_work_here` at all three counts, and its two anti-vacuity asserts (starts_with('('), contains("'sites'")) hold.

The NAMED CHECK is genuinely closed in guide_sync §8.4: renaming `TurnPhase::FivePowerBonus` from "5-Power bonus" to the superstring "5-Power bonuses" (describe.rs:305) FAILS `section8_phase_names_match_the_describer` — the `format!("`{name}`")` whole-cell match defeats the prefix mutation a bare `contains` would have passed.

Log-actor single-sourcing has grip: reverting `Session::apply` to `describe_move` (session.rs:500) fails THREE tests — `load_of_a_saved_session_reproduces_event_descriptions_exactly`, `the_captured_log_entries_are_driver_shaped_and_name_more_than_one_actor`, and the t11 capture set. `a_logged_move_names_its_actor_and_a_logged_reveal_does_not` (describe.rs:1318) is Eq-based, not substring.
The hidden-hand leak fence bites from the model outward: making `build_hand` populate cards regardless of `hidden` (screen_model.rs:2002) fails FOUR tests across screen_model, repl and view_render.
`NUMBER_BASE` is load-bearing and swept: flipping it 1 -> 0 fails 97 of 594 tests.

The card-entry parser's one-prefix discipline is pinned at the parser, not through a transcript: making an ambiguous good prefix resolve by list order (`[first, ..]`) FAILS `a_prefix_that_names_two_things_is_refused_not_guessed`, and the grammar matrix / refusal tests compare `CardEntry` by Eq rather than by substring.

The site-strip clip sweep bites at exactly the one column of margin it documents: adding a single space before the trading-house divider (board_render.rs:372) FAILS `no_registry_building_site_clips_its_slot_strip` over the 24-card x 16-built-state x owned/unowned sweep.

The per-count frame-width bound binds where the floor does not: raising `BELOW_BLOCK_MIN` 175 -> 177 fails FOUR tests (`frame_fits_the_raised_floor_at_every_player_count`, the real-game walk, the width-table pin, and the below-frame goldens) while staying well inside FLOOR_W.

The standing hint is pinned by many independent surfaces: rewording one clause ('help' for commands -> for the commands) fails 8 lib tests including both guide regeneration pins (`the_guide_movement_captures_are_what_the_fixtures_render`, `the_guide_opening_zone_capture_is_what_the_driver_renders`) and both frame goldens.

`next_edited`'s history contract holds without a terminal: deleting `editor.remember(&line)` FAILS `a_delivered_line_enters_the_history_and_an_abandoned_one_never_does`, whose `remembered == delivered` equality covers the paste-split and the Ctrl-C non-resurrection together.

The mid-group reveal conservation pin is an Eq over the pool-x-placements intersection (reveal.rs:810), not a substring guard, and the guided seat menu's refusals are pinned at `reveal_seat_choice` itself with Eq (repl.rs:7140-7151) — the T7 inner-parser lesson applied.
`section5_is_help_text_verbatim` (guide_sync.rs:567) compares the full normalized line vectors with an anti-vacuity length floor, so §5 is a property rather than the T12 audit's luck.

lenses.summary: Lens 4 (guide + document law). The pair is genuinely word-identical: my own independently written stripper reduces both halves to the same 72,632-char stream with zero diff blocks, §5 is byte-exact against HELP_TEXT in both formats, mkguide.py reproduces the committed .html byte-for-byte argument-free, and all six-plus regeneration pins pass.
